newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.514 billion yuan from 1.049 billion yuan with the seven-day contract the most actively traded.
Traders said trading was more active than Tuesday with both state banks and non-banking financial institutions trading more actively, encouraged by a healthy outlook for China's economy in 1997.
The China Securities newspaper quoted the State Statistical Bureau as saying that China's economic situation was good throughout the first half of 1997.
The newspaper said 1997 would see a record grain harvest so fund demand from grain-producing provinces would continue to increase over the next few weeks.
"Market sentiment was boosted by the newspaper report, with members trading more actively," said one trader.
"The interbank rates are likely to gain support from increased fund demand in the short term due to the approach of the summer harvest season," a second trader said.
"But falling inflation rates along with the improvement of the national economy are likely to exert downward pressure on the rates in the mid-term," he said.
